artifact.canonical_name: Modular Drive Architecture for Software-defined Vehicles Enabled by Power-packet-based Sensorless Control

sources.title: Modular Drive Architecture for Software-defined Vehicles Enabled by Power-packet-based Sensorless Control
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The proposed power-packet architecture moves motor state estimation and control logic to the vehicle side so the drive module can operate as a passive actuator commanded through information-tagged power packets.
The architecture is designed to eliminate local motor sensors/controllers and separate signal harnesses from the drive module, using a standardized packetized power interface instead.

A bench experiment with a 6/4 switched-reluctance motor verifies packet routing, hysteresis current control, current reconstruction and turn-off-angle detection using independent sensors only for validation.

metrics.name: approximate switching-angle detection delay
metrics.context: Authors attribute the delay to approximately 1-ms magnetizing intervals and discuss higher switching frequency as a mitigation.

limitations.text: Robust information-tag transmission under electromagnetic noise is identified as a practical requirement; error-correction redundancy was omitted from the experimental implementation.
The method assumes one excitation phase is magnetized at a time; simultaneous multi-phase excitation is future protocol work.
The experiment is a laboratory SRM/power-router bench, not an automotive drive-unit durability, EMC, fault-safety or production-vehicle validation.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Modular Drive Architecture for Software-defined Vehicles Enabled by Power-packet-based Sensorless Control; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full primary HTML verifies the passive-module/vehicle-side-control architecture, bench setup, 0.8-A reference/0.1-A band/24-V supply, current reconstruction, approximate 1-ms angle-detection delay, and noise/multi-phase limitations.

editorial.why_now_note: Although powertrain-specific, this work is a concrete example of a deeper zonal principle: move intelligence/state estimation inward and make edge modules standardized/passive where the physical interface permits.
editorial.rationale: Unusual but valuable architecture evidence for hardware/software boundary relocation and harness reduction; keep application-specific constraints explicit.
